definition_zh: 清单；名单；名册；列出；把……列入名单；（船）倾斜
definition_en: a series of items or names written down in order, an official register, the act of setting such items down, or, of a ship, a lean to one side
core_image: 一条窄纸条上，名字从上往下一行行排好
scene: 出门买菜前，她把要买的东西一项项写在纸条上，写完折好塞进外套口袋。Before leaving for the market, she read the shopping list one more time.
sceneCN: 这里 list 是「清单」（第 1 个义项：把事项逐条写下来的单子）；句意为出门去市场之前，她又看了一遍购物清单。画面里可抓住的物件：窄纸条、折痕、外套口袋。

pos.zh: 清单；名单；名册
列出；把……列入名单；（船）向一侧倾斜

derivatives.zh: 由 list 加 -ing 构成，指清单上的一条记录，也指挂牌信息或上市
由 list 的过去分词转作形容词，指已列入名单的、挂牌上市的
由 short 与 list 复合，指筛出的候选名单，或把人列入候选名单

senses.title: A series of items written down in order
senses.definition: a set of items, especially things to buy or do, written or printed one below another
senses.definitionCN: 把要买或要做的事项一条条写下来或印出来的单子
senses.example: She added eggs and bread to the shopping list.
senses.exampleCN: 她把鸡蛋和面包加进了购物清单。
senses.why: The oldest English list was not a page but a narrow strip of cloth or paper, an edge; once you write down such a strip, its shape alone turns the writing into a column of items, so the word moves from the material to what is written on it.
senses.whyCN: 古英语里 list 原指窄布条、纸条或边缘，而不是一整页；沿着这样的窄条往下写，光靠形状就把文字排成一列条目，于是词义从「材料」转到「写在上面的内容」。

senses.title: An official roll of names
senses.titleCN: 名册：为某一用途排好的名字
senses.definition: a register of names kept for a purpose, such as members, patients, or candidates
senses.definitionCN: 为某一用途保存的人名登记，如成员、病人或候选人名单
senses.example: The nurse checked the list of patients before the morning round.
senses.exampleCN: 护士在上午查房前核对了一遍病人名单。
senses.why: A strip of writing can be checked line by line, so institutions adopted the word for names kept in order; the list became a tool of record-keeping, which is why it appears with waiting, crew, and class.
senses.whyCN: 竖着写的窄条最适合一行行核对，机构便用这个词指按顺序保存的人名；list 由此成了登记工具，所以常与等候、船员、班级等词搭配。

senses.title: To set items or names down in order
senses.definition: to write or print items one after another, or to enter someone or something on an official record
senses.definitionCN: 把项目依次写出或印出，也指把某人某物登记进正式记录
senses.example: Please list the three books you found most useful.
senses.exampleCN: 请列出你觉得最有用的三本书。
senses.why: Because the noun already covered both the strip and the items on it, the verb needed no new shape: to list is simply to produce that column, whether on paper or in a database, and later to have one's name entered in a public record such as a stock exchange.
senses.whyCN: 名词已经同时指窄条和条上的条目，动词便不必另造形状：list 就是把这个竖列生产出来，无论写在纸上还是录进数据库；再往后，把名字登记进交易所这类公开记录也叫 list。

senses.title: Of a ship, to lean to one side
senses.definition: of a ship or boat, to lean or tilt to one side, especially because of wind, cargo, or damage
senses.definitionCN: 船或小艇因风、载重或破损而向一侧歪斜
senses.example: The old boat listed badly to port after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨过后，那条旧船严重向左舷倾斜。
senses.why: This nautical sense appears in the seventeenth century and its origin is uncertain; it may come from a Scandinavian word or from the older edge sense, and dictionaries treat it as a separate development that happens to share the spelling of the catalogue word.
senses.whyCN: 这个航海义项出现于十七世纪，来源不确定；它可能来自斯堪的纳维亚语，也可能与较早的「边缘」义有关，词典把它当作与「清单」同形而各自发展的一支。

intro.en: List began as a word for a narrow strip or edge; the catalogue sense may have come through French, and the nautical sense of leaning is of uncertain origin.
intro.cn: list 最初指窄条或边缘；「清单、名册」义可能经法语而来；表示船身倾斜的义项来源不确定。

items.en: *līstōn meant a strip, edge, or border; the asterisk marks a reconstructed form rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: *līstōn 意为窄条、边缘或边界；星号表示这是重构形式，并非有记录的原词。

items.en: Old English līste named the edge of cloth and later a strip of paper, the shape on which a column of writing fits.
items.cn: 古英语 līste 指布料边缘，后来也指纸条，正是竖排文字所依附的形状。

items.en: Old French liste, a roll or catalogue, may have strengthened the sense of a list of names; its own origin is uncertain and may be Germanic.
items.cn: 古法语的 liste 指名册或目录，可能强化了「名单」义；它本身的来源不确定，可能来自日耳曼语。

items.en: Middle English used liste for both the strip and the written roll, so the material and its contents merged.
items.cn: 中古英语的 liste 兼指窄条与写好的卷册，材料与内容由此合并。

items.en: Modern English keeps the noun for items and names, adds the verb to list, and keeps a separate nautical verb meaning to lean.
items.cn: 现代英语保留指条目与名字的名词，增加动词「列出」，并另有一个表示「倾斜」的航海动词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds and words spelled with list; the near-meaning group collects other words for ordered records.
note.cn: 形近组收含 list 的复合词与拼写相近的词；近义组收其他表示有序记录的词。

entries.definition: Without energy or enthusiasm; it comes from an old sense of list meaning desire, not from a catalogue.
entries.definitionCN: 无精打采的；它来自 list 表示「愿望」的古义，与清单无关，只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: To join the army, or to obtain help or support.
entries.definitionCN: 入伍；争取帮助或支持。

entries.definition: A list of things to be checked or done.
entries.definitionCN: 核对或待办事项的清单。

entries.definition: A small list of chosen candidates.
entries.definitionCN: 筛出的少量候选人名单。

entries.definition: A complete list of items, often arranged in a system.
entries.definitionCN: 完整而系统排列的目录。

entries.definition: A list of goods or property, often with counts.
entries.definitionCN: 货物或财产的清单，常带数量。

entries.definition: An official book or record of names and details.
entries.definitionCN: 正式登记姓名与信息的簿册。

entries.definition: A list of people and their duties or turns.
entries.definitionCN: 人员及其职责或轮值的名单。

normalIntro.en: The word is held together by an Old English noun for a strip and a French roll of names, with two English compounds built on it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由表示窄条的古英语名词与表示名册的法语词共同撑起，另有两个建立在它之上的英语复合词。

normal.en: The oldest list was a strip of cloth or paper, so picture a narrow column rather than a whole page.
normal.cn: 最早的 list 是一条窄布或窄纸，所以要想象一条竖直的窄栏，而不是一整页。

normal.en: List as a verb needs no new ending: the noun already held both the strip and the items.
normal.cn: list 作动词不必另加词尾：名词本身已经同时包含窄条与条目。

normal.en: Checklist and shortlist are list with a qualifier in front, one for checking and one for a chosen few.
normal.cn: checklist 与 shortlist 都是在 list 前面加限定成分，一个用于核对，一个用于精选。

normal.en: A waiting list is a queue written down, so the word keeps the idea of names arranged in order.
normal.cn: waiting list 就是写下来的队列，这个词始终保留「名字按顺序排列」的意思。

normal.en: The leaning ship uses the same spelling but a different history, so context decides which list you are reading.
normal.cn: 倾斜的船用的是同一拼写却有另一段历史，所以要看上下文判断读的是哪个 list。

abstract.en: A strip becomes a column, and a column becomes an institution's memory.
abstract.cn: 窄条变成竖栏，竖栏又变成机构的记忆。

abstract.en: To list is to decide what deserves a line and, by implication, what does not.
abstract.cn: 列出就是决定什么值得占一行，也等于决定什么不值得。

abstract.en: Two words can wear one spelling and still come from different places, as the ship and the catalogue show.
abstract.cn: 两个词可以共用一种拼写却来自不同地方，船与清单就是例子。

examples.en: She added eggs and bread to the shopping list.
examples.cn: 她把鸡蛋和面包加进了购物清单。

examples.en: The nurse checked the list of patients before the round.
examples.cn: 护士在查房前核对了病人名单。

examples.en: The boat listed to one side as the wind grew stronger.
examples.cn: 风越来越大，小船向一侧倾斜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「立事特」——要办的事立起来排成一条，就是清单；list 是清单、列出。

root: 古英语 līste（窄条、边缘）是这个词的起点；「清单、名册」义可能经古法语 liste 加强，来源不确定；「船身倾斜」为另一支，来源不确定。没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a narrow written column; from it come the item list, the official roll of names, the verb that produces them, and a separate nautical sense of leaning.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一条写满字的窄栏；由此分出事项清单、正式名册、产生清单的动词，以及另成一系的「船身倾斜」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow strip of paper with names written down it, one under another.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条窄纸条，名字从上往下一行行写下去。

branches.cn: 一只手在竖栏里添上新的一行

branches.cn: 渔船的船身严重向左舷倾斜

intro.en: The word is supported by an Old English noun for a strip, a French roll of names, and two English compounds built on list.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示窄条的古英语名词、表示名册的法语词，以及两个建立在 list 之上的英语复合词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin lista is a borrowing from Germanic or Old French, so no native Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 lista 借自日耳曼语或古法语，因此这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 听；倾听；听从；留心等着听；偷听
definition_en: to give deliberate attention to sound, to heed what is said, to wait for a particular sound, or to overhear a conversation
core_image: 一个人停下手里的活，侧耳朝向声音来源
scene: 夜里屋子很静，母亲关掉电视，侧耳对着楼上婴儿床的方向。She turned down the radio and listened for the baby's cry.
sceneCN: 这里 listen 是「留心等着听」（第 3 个义项：等某个声音出现）；句意为她调低收音机，等着听婴儿的哭声。画面里可抓住的物件：关掉的电视、楼上的婴儿床、调低的音量。

pos.zh: 听；倾听；听从；留心等着听；偷听

derivatives.zh: 由 listen 加 -er 构成，指听的人，尤指收听节目的听众
由 listen 加 -ing 构成，指听的行为，也指用心倾听的
由 listen 加 -able 构成，指听着不难受、值得一听的

senses.title: To give attention to sound
senses.titleCN: 听：把注意力放到声音上
senses.definition: to give deliberate attention to a sound or to someone speaking
senses.definitionCN: 有意识地把注意力放在某个声音或某人的说话上
senses.example: She listened to the rain on the roof until she fell asleep.
senses.exampleCN: 她听着屋顶上的雨声，直到睡着。
senses.why: Old English had hlysnan for attending to sound beside hyran for simply hearing; the two verbs split the work, and listen took the side of effort and attention rather than passive reception.
senses.whyCN: 古英语里 hlysnan 表示注意地听，hyran 表示听见；两个动词分工，listen 占了「费心去听」这一边，而不是被动接收。

senses.title: To heed advice or a warning
senses.titleCN: 听从：把听到的话当回事
senses.definition: to pay attention to advice, a warning, or a request and act on it
senses.definitionCN: 重视劝告、警告或请求并照着去做
senses.example: He never listens to his doctor about sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 他从不听医生关于睡眠的建议。
senses.why: Hearing turns into obedience when the listener acts on what was said; the same verb slides from the ear to behaviour, which is why listen to reason and listen to your parents sound natural.
senses.whyCN: 当听的人照着话去做，听见就变成了服从；同一个动词从耳朵滑到行为，所以 listen to reason（听劝）和听父母的话都很自然。

senses.title: To wait and watch for a particular sound
senses.titleCN: 留心等着听：等某个声音出现
senses.definition: to keep one's attention on the possibility of a particular sound, especially in order to respond
senses.definitionCN: 把注意力放在某个可能出现的声响上，以便及时反应
senses.example: The guard listened for footsteps on the stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 守卫留神听着楼梯上的脚步声。
senses.why: The preposition for turns listening into a search: nothing has been heard yet, and the ear is held open for a signal, as in listen for the doorbell.
senses.whyCN: 介词 for 把「听」变成「找」：此刻还没有声音，只是把耳朵开着等一个信号，如留神听门铃。

senses.title: To overhear others on purpose
senses.titleCN: 偷听：躲在暗处听别人说话
senses.definition: to hear a conversation that is not meant for you, often by staying hidden or by using a device
senses.definitionCN: 听到并非说给自己听的谈话，常靠躲藏或借助设备
senses.example: Someone was listening in on the meeting from the next room.
senses.exampleCN: 有人躲在隔壁房间偷听会议。
senses.why: The particle in adds the idea of entering a space that is not yours, so listen in on marks the listener as an outsider who was never invited.
senses.whyCN: 小品词 in 加进「进入不属于自己的空间」的意思，所以 listen in on 把听者标成未被邀请的外人。

intro.en: Listen goes back to a Germanic verb for hearing with attention; the h of its Old English form was later dropped, and the word is widely linked to the root behind loud.
intro.cn: listen 源自日耳曼语中表示「用心听」的动词；古英语形式里的 h 后来被丢掉，一般认为它与 loud 同源。

items.en: The reconstructed root *ḱlew- meant to hear, and it also underlies words for fame, since being heard of is being talked about.
items.cn: 重构词根 *ḱlew- 意为「听见」，也衍生出表示名声的词，因为被人听说就是被人谈论。

items.en: *hlusinōn, a verb of listening, grew beside *hlūdaz, the adjective that became loud; both point back to the act of hearing.
items.cn: *hlusinōn 是表示「听」的动词，与后来变成 loud 的形容词 *hlūdaz 并生；两者都指向「听见」这一行为。

items.en: Old English wrote the verb as hlysnan, with an h that speakers later stopped pronouncing.
items.cn: 古英语把动词写作 hlysnan，词首的 h 后来在口语中不再发音。

items.en: Middle English settled on listen, dropped the h in spelling, and kept the meaning of giving ear to something.
items.cn: 中古英语定型为 listen，拼写中去掉 h，保留「把耳朵给某物」的意思。

items.en: Modern English adds listener and listening, and the phrasal forms listen in and listen up, which push the word toward eavesdropping and toward a call for attention.
items.cn: 现代英语派生 listener 与 listening，并发展出 listen in、listen up 等短语，把词义推向偷听与提醒注意。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built with listen; the near-meaning group separates deliberate listening from mere hearing and from related acts of attention.
note.cn: 形近组收由 listen 构成的词形；近义组把刻意的「听」与单纯的「听见」以及相关的注意行为区分开。

entries.definition: A person who listens, especially to a radio programme.
entries.definitionCN: 听的人；收听节目的听众。

entries.definition: The act of paying attention to sound, or an adjective for such activity.
entries.definitionCN: 听的行为；用心倾听的。

entries.definition: Pleasant or easy enough to listen to.
entries.definitionCN: 听着不难受、值得一听的。

entries.definition: A written series of items or names; the two words are only close in spelling and sound, with different origins.
entries.definitionCN: 写下来的条目或名单；与 listen 只是拼写发音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To receive sound, often without deliberate attention.
entries.definitionCN: 听见，常指并非刻意去听。

entries.definition: To pay careful attention to advice or a warning.
entries.definitionCN: 留意并重视劝告或警告。

entries.definition: To hear something by chance, without intending to.
entries.definitionCN: 无意中听到。

entries.definition: To listen secretly to a private conversation.
entries.definitionCN: 偷听私人谈话。

normalIntro.en: The word is carried by an Old English verb, its lost h, a Germanic root shared with loud, and English endings that make a listener and a listening.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由古英语动词、失落了的 h、与 loud 共有的日耳曼词根，以及构成 listener 与 listening 的英语词尾共同支撑。

normal.en: Old English wrote the verb with an h, so the silent letter in today's spelling is a leftover, not a rule about pronunciation.
normal.cn: 古英语写法带 h，所以今天拼写里的不发音字母是遗留物，并不是发音规则。

normal.en: Listener is listen plus -er, the person at the receiving end of the sound.
normal.cn: listener 是 listen 加 -er，指声音接收端的那个人。

normal.en: Hear is what happens to you; listen is what you decide to do, and English keeps both verbs.
normal.cn: hear 是发生在你身上的事，listen 是你决定去做的事，英语把两个动词都保留下来。

normal.en: Listen for waits for a signal; listen to receives what is already there; the preposition marks the difference.
normal.cn: listen for 是等一个信号，listen to 是接收已经在那里的声音，介词标出了这个差别。

normal.en: Listen in on adds in because the listener steps into a space where he was not invited.
normal.cn: listen in on 之所以加 in，是因为听者走进了没有邀请他的空间。

abstract.en: To listen is to lend someone your ears for a while, which is why the verb so easily turns into obedience.
abstract.cn: 倾听是把耳朵借给别人一段时间，所以这个动词很容易变成服从。

abstract.en: Attention has a direction: you can listen to, listen for, or listen in, and each preposition draws a different boundary.
abstract.cn: 注意力是有方向的：可以 listen to、listen for、listen in，每个介词都画出不同的边界。

abstract.en: A word for hearing can grow into a word for trust, because people who are heard are also more likely to be followed.
abstract.cn: 表示「听」的词能长成表示「信任」的词，因为被听见的人也更容易被跟随。

examples.en: She listened to the rain until she fell asleep.
examples.cn: 她听着雨声直到睡着。

examples.en: The guard listened for footsteps on the stairs.
examples.cn: 守卫留神听着楼梯上的脚步声。

examples.en: He never listens to his doctor.
examples.cn: 他从不听医生的劝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「力森」——用力把声音收进耳朵，就是倾听；listen 是听。

root: 古英语 hlysnan（用心听）来自日耳曼语 *hlusinōn，词首 h 后来失落；一般认为与 loud 同源，并可上溯到重构词根 *ḱlew-（听见）；拉丁语 cluere（闻名）也出自这一词根，只是词义已转向「被谈论」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is deliberate attention to sound; it divides into obedience to what is said, waiting for a signal, and listening where one is not welcome.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是刻意把注意力放在声音上；由此分出听从所说的话、等候某个信号，以及在不被欢迎的地方偷听。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person stopping work and turning one ear toward the source of a sound.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人停下手里的活，侧耳朝向声音的来源。

branches.en: a head tilted toward rain on a roof
branches.cn: 头侧向屋顶的雨声

branches.en: an ear kept open while nothing is heard yet
branches.cn: 什么都还没听见，耳朵却已经开着

branches.en: a patient nodding at the doctor's advice
branches.cn: 病人对医生的嘱咐点头

branches.en: a guard holding still for footsteps
branches.cn: 守卫静止不动等脚步声

intro.cn: 这个词由古英语动词、失落的 h、与 loud 共有的日耳曼词根，以及构成 listener 与 listening 的英语后缀支撑。

latinIntro.en: The same reconstructed root is thought to lie behind Latin cluere 'to be spoken of' and its adjective inclutus 'famous', where hearing has shifted into reputation.

definition_zh: 升（公制容积单位）；一升的量；以升计的发动机排量
definition_en: the metric unit of volume equal to one cubic decimetre, a quantity of that size, or the same unit used for engine displacement
core_image: 透明量杯里，液面停在标着升数的刻度上
scene: 厨房里，厨师把牛奶倒进量杯，瓶身上的容量标注正好对齐刻度。A single liter of milk was enough for the whole batter.
sceneCN: 这里 liter 是「一升的量」（第 2 个义项：按升计的一份液体）；句意是一升牛奶就够和这一整盆面糊。画面里可抓住的物件：量杯、瓶身容量标注、对齐的刻度。

pos.zh: 升（公制容积单位）；一升的量；以升计的排量

derivatives.zh: liter 的英式拼写，源自法语 litre，含义完全相同
由 milli-（千分之一）加 liter 构成，指毫升
由 kilo-（千）加 liter 构成，指千升

senses.title: The metric unit of volume
senses.definition: the metric unit of volume equal to one cubic decimetre, used for liquids, gases, and loose dry goods
senses.definitionCN: 公制容积单位，等于一立方分米，用于液体、气体以及松散干物
senses.example: The tank holds forty liters of water.
senses.exampleCN: 这个水箱能装四十升水。
senses.why: The word entered English together with the metric system, which gave volume a decimal unit; a litre is defined as the space inside a cube ten centimetres on each side, so the size is fixed by geometry rather than by any bottle.
senses.whyCN: 这个词随公制一起进入英语，公制为容积设定了十进制的单位；一升定义为一个十厘米见方的立方体内部的容积，因此大小由几何确定，而不是由某个瓶子决定。

senses.title: A quantity of that size, especially of a drink or fuel
senses.titleCN: 一升的量：按升卖的一份
senses.definition: a quantity of liquid amounting to one liter, especially as sold or poured
senses.definitionCN: 等于一升的液体量，尤指售卖或倒出的一份
senses.example: He bought a liter of milk on the way home.
senses.exampleCN: 他回家路上买了一升牛奶。
senses.why: Once the unit is fixed, it can count portions instead of only measuring them; shopkeepers and cooks say a liter of milk the way others say a bottle or a cup, and the unit takes a plural.
senses.whyCN: 单位一旦固定，就可以用来数「份」而不只是测量；店家与厨师说一升牛奶，就像别人说一瓶、一杯，这个单位也就能变复数。

senses.title: A unit for engine displacement
senses.titleCN: 排量：以升计的气缸容积
senses.definition: the same unit used to state the total volume swept by the pistons of an engine, as in a two-liter engine
senses.definitionCN: 同一单位用于表示发动机活塞扫过的总容积，如「两升发动机」
senses.example: The car has a small one-liter engine.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆车配的是一台小型一升发动机。
senses.why: Engine size is itself a volume, so the same unit travels from the kitchen to the garage; a two-liter engine is an engine whose cylinders sweep two liters of air in one cycle.
senses.whyCN: 发动机排量本身就是容积，所以同一单位从厨房走进车库；两升发动机就是气缸在一个循环里扫过两升空气的发动机。

intro.en: Liter came into English through French from a Latin borrowing of a Greek unit name; the American spelling dropped the British re ending.
intro.cn: liter 经法语进入英语，源头是拉丁语对希腊单位名的借用；美式拼写省去了英式的 re 词尾。

items.en: The Greek word litra named a Sicilian unit of weight and, by extension, of capacity; its own earlier origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 希腊语 litra 指西西里的一种重量单位，也引申指容量单位；它更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Latin borrowed the word as litra, still a unit of weight, and passed it on to the languages of western Europe.
items.cn: 拉丁语借作 litra，仍作重量单位，并把它传进西欧诸语言。

items.en: Old French used litre for a measure of capacity, and French kept the word when the metric system was created.
items.cn: 古法语用 litre 表示一种容量单位，法国在创立公制时保留了这个词。

items.en: English adopted litre along with metric measures in the nineteenth century, spelled in the French way.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪随公制一起引入 litre，并按法语方式拼写。

items.en: American usage settled on liter, while British usage keeps litre; compounds such as milliliter and kiloliter follow the American form in the United States.
items.cn: 美式用法定型为 liter，英式仍作 litre；milliliter、kiloliter 等复合词在美国跟随美式写法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the British spelling and near spellings with different histories; the near-meaning group collects other units and words for volume.
note.cn: 形近组收英式拼写与历史无关的近似拼写；近义组收其他单位以及表示容积的词。

entries.definition: The British spelling of the same unit, with no difference in meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 同一单位的英式拼写，含义没有差别。

entries.definition: A written symbol or a written message; it is only close in spelling, with a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 字母或信件；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A unit of length, or a measuring device; the spelling is close but the word is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 长度单位或计量仪表；拼写相近，但词源无关。

entries.definition: One thousandth of a liter.
entries.definitionCN: 千分之一升；毫升。

entries.definition: A larger unit of liquid volume used in Britain and America.
entries.definitionCN: 英美使用的一种较大液体容量单位。

entries.definition: A quarter of a gallon, used for milk and other liquids.
entries.definitionCN: 四分之一加仑，用于牛奶等液体。

entries.definition: A smaller unit of liquid volume, about half a quart.
entries.definitionCN: 较小的液体容量单位，约半夸脱。

entries.definition: The amount of space that something occupies.
entries.definitionCN: 物体所占空间的大小；体积。

normalIntro.en: The word arrived through Greek, Latin and French already carrying a measuring habit, and its spelling split between litre and liter.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词经希腊语、拉丁语和法语传来时已经带着测量的习惯，后来拼写在 litre 与 liter 之间分家。

normal.en: The Greek unit litra came through Latin and French, so the word arrived already carrying a measuring habit.
normal.cn: 希腊单位 litra 经拉丁语和法语传来，所以这个词到达英语时已经带着测量的习惯。

normal.en: Liter and litre are the same unit; only the ending differs between American and British spelling.
normal.cn: liter 与 litre 是同一个单位，只是美式与英式拼写的词尾不同。

normal.en: Milliliter puts milli-, one thousandth, in front of liter, so the unit shrinks by three decimal places.
normal.cn: milliliter 在 liter 前加表示千分之一的 milli-，单位缩小了三位小数。

normal.en: Kiloliter adds kilo-, one thousand, at the other end of the scale.
normal.cn: kiloliter 在刻度另一端加上表示一千的 kilo-。

normal.en: Because a liter is a volume, the same word measures milk, petrol and the cylinders of an engine.
normal.cn: 既然升是容积，同一个词就能量牛奶、汽油和发动机气缸。

abstract.en: A unit is a promise that everyone will cut the world the same way.
abstract.cn: 单位是一种承诺：所有人都用同样的方式切割世界。

abstract.en: Decimal measures travel easily because each step is a power of ten, which is why liter fits so neatly with milli- and kilo-.
abstract.cn: 十进制的度量容易传播，因为每一步都是十的幂，所以 liter 与 milli-、kilo- 配合得严丝合缝。

abstract.en: The same liter can sit in a kitchen, a fuel pump or an engine bay, and the number stays comparable.
abstract.cn: 同一升可以出现在厨房、油泵或发动机舱，数字始终可比。

examples.en: He bought a liter of milk on the way home.
examples.cn: 他回家路上买了一升牛奶。

examples.en: The tank holds forty liters of water.
examples.cn: 这个水箱能装四十升水。

examples.en: The car has a one-liter engine.
examples.cn: 这辆车配的是一升发动机。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「利特」——瓶上印着利落的特制刻度，一升就是 liter。

root: 希腊语 litra（西西里重量、容量单位）经拉丁语 litra 与法语 litre 进入英语；美式写作 liter，英式写作 litre。与表示「字母、信件」的 letter 只是拼写相近，词源无关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is one metric unit of volume; it extends to a poured quantity, and then to engine size, which is measured in the same unit.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一个公制容积单位；它延伸到倒出的一份液体，再延伸到同样以容积计量的发动机排量。

core.cn: 核心意象：透明量杯里，液面停在标着升数的刻度线上。

intro.en: The word is a chain of borrowings, running from a Greek unit through Latin and French to the two modern spellings, with metric prefixes building the larger and smaller units.
intro.cn: 这个词是一串借用：从希腊单位经拉丁语、法语到两种现代拼写，再由公制前缀造出更大和更小的单位。

latinIntro.en: Latin litra is not a native Latin root but a borrowing of Greek litra, so the line of descent runs from Greek through Latin and French into English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 litra 不是拉丁本土词根，而是对希腊语 litra 的借用，所以传承线从希腊语经拉丁语、法语进入英语。

definition_zh: 按字面；逐字地；确实地；简直（口语夸张用法）
definition_en: in a literal sense or word for word, in fact, or, informally, as a strong intensifier with little literal truth
core_image: 手指沿着印刷的一行字，一个字母一个字母移过去
scene: 朋友把一句玩笑当成真话，还认真追问细节，旁边的人忍不住笑。She took his joke literally and began checking the figures.
sceneCN: 这里 literally 是「按字面」（第 1 个义项：照词语本义理解）；句意是她把玩笑按字面当真，开始核对数字。画面里可抓住的动作：朋友认真追问、旁人的笑、纸上待核对的数字。

pos.zh: 按字面；逐字地；确实地；简直

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 littera（字母）加 -al 构成，指字面的、照字面理解的
由 literal 加 -ness 构成，指拘泥字面的性质
由 literal 加 -ism 构成，指拘泥字面、字面主义的做法

senses.title: In the literal sense of the words
senses.titleCN: 按字面：照词语本来的意思
senses.definition: in the ordinary, literal meaning of the words used, rather than in a figurative or exaggerated one
senses.definitionCN: 按所用词语的本义去理解，而不是按比喻或夸张的意思
senses.example: The phrase was meant literally, not as a joke.
senses.exampleCN: 这句话是按字面意思说的，不是开玩笑。
senses.why: The word is built on Latin littera, a letter of the alphabet, so literally begins as 'according to the letters': you read what the words actually say, and no picture is allowed to stand in for them.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在拉丁语 littera（字母）之上，literally 的起点是「按照字母」：你读的是词语实际写出的内容，不许任何比喻顶替它。

senses.title: Word for word
senses.definition: word for word, following the exact order and wording of the original
senses.definitionCN: 逐字照原话的顺序与措辞，不作改动
senses.example: The contract was translated literally, so the jokes disappeared.
senses.exampleCN: 合同是逐字翻译的，所以笑话全没了。
senses.why: If you follow the letters one by one, you also follow the words in their original order; translation done this way keeps the surface and loses the idiom.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个字母一个字母地跟着走，也就按原来的顺序跟着词走；这样翻译保住了表面，却丢掉了习语。

senses.title: In fact, really
senses.titleCN: 确实地：强调事情真的发生
senses.definition: actually, really, without exaggeration, used to stress that something surprising is true
senses.definitionCN: 确实、真的，不带夸张，用来强调某件令人意外的事是真的
senses.example: The team literally ran out of paper on the last day.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在最后一天确实把纸用完了。
senses.why: Because 'according to the letters' means 'according to the facts as stated', the adverb can certify a statement: what sounds like an exaggeration is being claimed as plain truth.
senses.whyCN: 既然「按字面」就是「按写明的事实」，这个副词就能为陈述作证：听起来像夸张的话，其实是在说大实话。

senses.title: As an intensifier, almost
senses.titleCN: 口语夸张用法：简直、几乎（并不字面）
senses.definition: used in informal speech as a strong intensifier, often when the statement is not literally true
senses.definitionCN: 口语中作强烈的加强词，常用于所述并非字面真实的情况
senses.example: I literally died laughing at that video.
senses.exampleCN: 那个视频简直把我笑死了。
senses.why: Intensifiers wear out and are borrowed from stronger words; speakers reached for literally to mark emphasis, and the very word for exactness became a badge of exaggeration, a usage dictionaries now record.
senses.whyCN: 加强词会磨损，于是从更有力的词里借用；说话人抓来 literally 表示强调，结果这个专管精确的词反倒成了夸张的标记，词典如今已收录这种用法。

intro.en: Literally is an English adverb built on literal, which descends from Latin littera, a letter of the alphabet.
intro.cn: literally 是英语副词，建立在 literal 之上，而 literal 源自拉丁语 littera（字母）。

items.en: Littera meant a letter of the alphabet, and in the plural litterae it could mean a letter, a document, or learning.
items.cn: littera 指字母，复数 litterae 可指书信、文书或学问。

items.en: Late Latin litteralis meant 'of letters' and described meaning that stays with the written words.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 litteralis 意为「字母的」，用来描述紧贴字面文字的涵义。

items.en: English took literal in the fifteenth century for meaning that follows the letter rather than the spirit.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪引入 literal，指跟随字面而非精神的理解。

items.en: Literally was formed with -ly soon after, first for word-for-word rendering and then for stating plain fact.
items.cn: literally 随后由 -ly 构成，先表逐字表达，再表陈述直白的事实。

items.en: In the twentieth century the intensifier use spread in speech, and it is now recorded, though still criticised in formal writing.
items.cn: 二十世纪里，加强语气的用法在口语中扩散，如今已被收录，但在正式写作中仍有争议。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin stem for letter; the near-meaning group collects adverbs of exactness and reality.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「字母」词干上的词；近义组收表示精确与真实的副词。

entries.definition: Following the basic meaning of the words.
entries.definitionCN: 按词语本义的；字面的。

entries.definition: The ability to read and write, built on the same stem for letters.
entries.definitionCN: 读写能力，同样建立在「字母」词干上。

entries.definition: Written works, from the same stem as letters.
entries.definitionCN: 文学作品，与「字母」同一词干。

entries.definition: A written symbol or message, from the same Latin word.
entries.definitionCN: 字母或书信，来自同一个拉丁词。

entries.definition: Relating to literature or written language.
entries.definitionCN: 与文学或书面语言有关的。

entries.definition: In a precise way, with nothing added or left out.
entries.definitionCN: 精确地，不增不减。

entries.definition: In fact, as opposed to what was expected.
entries.definitionCN: 事实上，与预期相对。

entries.definition: In a genuine or sincere way.
entries.definitionCN: 真正地；真诚地。

entries.definition: In effect or almost, though not strictly.
entries.definitionCN: 实际上；几乎，虽非严格如此。

normalIntro.en: Literal comes from a Latin noun for a letter, so the adverb is a word about reading the letters in front of you.
normalIntro.cn: literal 来自拉丁语中表示字母的名词，所以这个副词是一个关于「读眼前字母」的词。

normal.en: Literal comes from littera, a letter, so a literal reading stays with the letters in front of you.
normal.cn: literal 来自 littera（字母），所以字面阅读就是紧跟着眼前的字母。

normal.en: Add -ly and the adjective becomes the adverb that says how the reading is done.
normal.cn: 加上 -ly，形容词就变成说明「怎样读」的副词。

normal.en: Translate literally is word for word; translate freely is by sense, and the two labels mark opposite choices.
normal.cn: 逐字翻译是跟着词走，意译是跟着意思走，两个说法标出相反的选择。

normal.en: Literally true certifies a surprising fact, so the word is doing the work of really.
normal.cn: literally true 是在为一件意外的事实作证，这个词在做 really 的活。

normal.en: A sentence like I literally died is not literal at all, which shows the intensifier has drifted from its root.
normal.cn: 像「我简直死了」这样的句子一点也不是字面意思，可见这个加强词已经漂离了词根。

abstract.en: A word built on letters becomes a word for truth, and then for emphasis, and the direction of travel is worth noticing.
abstract.cn: 一个建立在字母上的词变成了表示真实的词，又变成加强词，这个移动方向值得注意。

abstract.en: Exactness is a surface; when a sentence is read only at the surface, the joke or the metaphor is lost.
abstract.cn: 精确只是表面；只按表面读一句话，玩笑或隐喻就丢了。

abstract.en: The strongest claim of literalness can end up producing the least literal sentence.
abstract.cn: 最卖力声称字面的一句话，可能恰恰最不字面。

examples.en: The phrase was meant literally, not as a joke.
examples.cn: 这句话是按字面意思说的，不是玩笑。

examples.en: The contract was translated literally.
examples.cn: 这份合同是逐字翻译的。

examples.en: The team literally ran out of paper.
examples.cn: 团队确实把纸用完了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「李特柔利」——把每个字都照原样读出来，literally 是字面地。

root: 拉丁语 littera（字母）→ 晚期拉丁语 litteralis（字母的；字面的）→ 英语 literal → 加 -ly 成 literally；核心义「按字面」，后发展出「确实」与口语夸张用法。

sensesIntro.en: The core is reading by the letters; it branches into word-for-word rendering, into certifying plain fact, and into the looser intensifier use of speech.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是照着字母读；由此分出逐字翻译、为事实作证，以及口语里较松的夸张加强用法。

core.cn: 核心意象：手指沿着印刷的一行字，一个字母一个字母地移过去。

branches.cn: 读者停在页面上确切的词句

branches.en: a translator following the original word by word

branches.cn: 词与它如今声称的东西之间的缝

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun littera and its derivative adjective litteralis supply the whole family, and English keeps the stem in literal, literary and literature.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 littera 及其派生形容词 litteralis 提供了整族词，英语在 literal、literary 与 literature 里保留了这一词干。

senses.title: Relating to literature
senses.definition: connected with literature, especially novels, poems and plays that are valued as art
senses.definitionCN: 与文学有关的，尤指与被视为艺术的小说、诗歌和戏剧有关
senses.example: She has a keen literary taste and reads a novel every week.
senses.exampleCN: 她文学品味敏锐，每周读一本小说。
senses.why: Latin littera meant a letter of the alphabet, and writing made of letters grew into literature; literary simply points back to that body of writing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 littera 意为字母，由字母写成的文字逐渐长成文学；literary 就是回头指向这一整片写作。

senses.title: Typical of formal written language
senses.definition: of a word or style, formal and at home in books rather than in ordinary conversation
senses.definitionCN: 指词语或文风正式，常见于书本，而不用于日常对话
senses.example: The word behold is literary rather than conversational.
senses.exampleCN: behold 这个词是书面语，而不是日常口语。
senses.why: A word that has left the street but survives in books is labelled by the place where it still lives; literary records the shelf, not the age of the word.
senses.whyCN: 一个词从街头消失却仍在书中存活，就被按它如今的栖身之处来标注；literary 记下的是书架，不是这个词的年岁。

senses.title: Having the quality of artful writing
senses.definition: showing the imagination and craft associated with good literature
senses.definitionCN: 显出与优秀文学作品相联系的想象力与写作技艺
senses.example: His account of the journey has a literary quality that makes it memorable.
senses.exampleCN: 他对这次旅程的记述有一种文学性的质地，让人读过难忘。
senses.why: Literature is writing judged for craft as well as content; when a passage invites that judgment, the adjective follows it from the shelf into the sentence.
senses.whyCN: 文学是既看内容也看手笔的文字；当一段话引来这种品评时，这个形容词便跟着它从书架走进句子，形容那段文字本身的质地。

senses.title: Connected with the profession of letters
senses.titleCN: 从事文学的；文学工作的
senses.definition: involving writers, books and the business or study that surrounds them, as in a literary agent or a literary magazine
senses.definitionCN: 涉及作家、书籍以及围绕它们的行业或研究，如文学经纪人、文学杂志
senses.example: The literary agent read the manuscript and offered a contract.
senses.exampleCN: 那位文学经纪人读完稿子，给了出版合同。
senses.why: Books support a small industry of editors, agents and magazines; literary names that professional world because it exists to produce and sell literature.
senses.whyCN: 书籍养活了编辑、经纪人和杂志组成的小行业；literary 指的就是这个职业圈子，因为它的存在就是为了生产和销售文学。

intro.en: Literary descends from the Latin word for a letter, and it still points to writing that is made of letters and valued as art.
intro.cn: literary 源自拉丁语中表示「字母」的词，至今仍指向由字母写成、并被当作艺术来欣赏的文字。

items.en: Littera named a letter of the alphabet, and in the plural it could name a written document or an epistle.
items.cn: littera 指字母表中的一个字母，复数形式还可指文书或书信。

items.en: The adjective litterarius meant of letters or of writing, and it covered both the skill of reading and the study of texts.
items.cn: 形容词 litterarius 意为与字母、书写有关的，既指读写技能，也指对文本的研究。

items.en: Old French reshaped the Latin adjective as literaire, keeping the sense of letters, learning and written culture.
items.cn: 古法语把拉丁形容词改写为 literaire，保留了文字、学问与书面文化的意味。

items.en: English borrowed the French form as literary in the seventeenth century, when literature was coming to mean fine writing rather than learning in general.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语借入法语形式，写作 literary；当时 literature 正从泛指学问转向指精美的写作。

items.en: Modern English keeps literary for the art of writing, for its formal register, and for the people and institutions that surround books.
items.cn: 现代英语用 literary 指写作的艺术、其正式语体，以及围绕书籍的人和机构。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin word for a letter; the near-meaning group gathers words for writing, art and books.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「字母」一词上的词；近义组收表示写作、艺术与书籍的词。

normalIntro.en: The word is anchored in the Latin name for a letter, and its family keeps returning to reading, writing and the art of books.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词锚定在拉丁语对「字母」的称呼上，它的同族词反复回到阅读、书写与书本的艺术。

normal.en: Latin littera is a letter, so literature is writing made of letters and literary is what belongs to that writing.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 littera 是字母，所以 literature 是由字母写成的文字，literary 则指属于这种文字的东西。

normal.en: Literature and literary share one stem: the noun names the whole body of works, the adjective describes what belongs to it.
normal.cn: literature 与 literary 共用一个词干：名词指整批作品，形容词描述属于这批作品的东西。

normal.en: Literate and literacy also come from the letter, because knowing the letters is the first step into reading.
normal.cn: literate 与 literacy 也来自「字母」，因为认识字母是进入阅读的第一步。

normal.en: A literary agent handles books as a business, so the adjective also names the profession built around literature.
normal.cn: 文学经纪人把书当作生意来经营，所以这个形容词也指围绕文学形成的职业。

normal.en: Call a word literary when you meet it mainly in books, because the label records where the word still lives.
normal.cn: 一个词若主要是在书里遇到，就叫它 literary，因为这个标签记下的是它如今还住在哪里。

abstract.en: Letters are small marks that carry whole worlds, and literary is the adjective for the world built out of those marks.
abstract.cn: 字母是承载整个世界的小小记号，literary 就是形容由这些记号搭起来的那个世界。

abstract.en: A page can be read for information or for beauty; literary marks the second use.
abstract.cn: 一页纸可以为了信息去读，也可以为了美去读；literary 标出的是后一种读法。

abstract.en: Every literature begins with someone learning a handful of letters, which is why the same root also names literacy.
abstract.cn: 每一部文学都从有人学会几个字母开始，所以同一个词根也用来指读写能力。

senses.title: Written works valued as art
senses.definition: novels, poems, plays and other writing valued for form and imagination rather than for information alone
senses.definitionCN: 小说、诗歌、戏剧等因其形式与想象力而受重视、而非只用来传递信息的写作
senses.example: She studied English literature at university.
senses.exampleCN: 她在大学学习英国文学。
senses.why: Litteratura first meant the act of writing and the learning that letters bring; the works carrying that learning took the name, and artistic writing moved to the centre.
senses.whyCN: litteratura 最初指书写这件事以及文字带来的学问；承载这种学问的作品接过了这个名字，艺术性的写作后来占据了中心。

senses.title: The body of writing on a subject
senses.definition: the books, articles and reports published about a particular subject, considered as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 关于某一主题已出版的书籍、文章与报告的整体
senses.example: The literature on climate change is now enormous.
senses.exampleCN: 关于气候变化的文献现在多得惊人。
senses.why: A subject keeps its knowledge in texts; once those texts pile up, scholars call the whole shelf the literature of the field, even when the writing is technical.
senses.whyCN: 一个学科把知识存放在文本里；文本一旦堆积起来，学者就把整排书架称作该领域的文献，即便那些文字是技术性的。

senses.title: The academic study of literary works
senses.definition: the subject taught and researched at universities that deals with novels, poems and plays
senses.definitionCN: 大学里讲授与研究小说、诗歌、戏剧的学科
senses.example: He teaches literature at a small college.
senses.exampleCN: 他在一所小学规模的学院教文学。
senses.why: A body of texts large enough to be taught turns into a subject; the noun for the works becomes the noun for the department that studies them.
senses.whyCN: 一批文本大到可以被讲授时，就变成了一个学科；指作品的名词于是也用来指研究这些作品的院系。

senses.title: Printed material used for promotion
senses.definition: leaflets, brochures and other printed matter used to advertise or explain something
senses.definitionCN: 用来宣传或说明某事的传单、小册子等印刷品
senses.example: The clinic sent promotional literature to every household.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所给每户人家都寄了宣传资料。
senses.why: Print carries authority, so advertisers borrowed the word for their brochures; a leaflet inherits the seriousness of a book even when it is selling soap.
senses.whyCN: 印刷品自带权威感，于是广告商借这个词来指自己的小册子；一张传单即便在推销肥皂，也继承了书本的严肃。

intro.en: Literature comes from a Latin word for writing and learning, and only later narrowed towards novels, poems and plays.
intro.cn: literature 来自拉丁语中表示书写与学问的词，后来才收窄到指小说、诗歌与戏剧。

items.en: Littera meant a letter of the alphabet, and the plural litterae often meant a written document or a letter sent to someone.
items.cn: littera 指字母表中的一个字母，复数 litterae 常指文书或寄给人的书信。

items.en: Litteratura named writing and the learning gained from letters, but not yet a shelf of novels.
items.cn: litteratura 指书写活动以及由文字得来的学问，那时还不指一整架小说。

items.en: Old French took the word as literature, still meaning learning and written culture rather than fiction.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词写作 literature，仍指学问与书面文化，而不是虚构故事。

items.en: Early English used literature for polite learning and scholarship; the modern sense of imaginative writing developed slowly.
items.cn: 早期英语用 literature 指文雅的学问与学术；指想象性写作的现代义项是慢慢发展出来的。

items.en: Modern English centres literature on novels, poems and plays, while keeping the older sense for the body of writing on any subject.
items.cn: 现代英语把 literature 的中心放在小说、诗歌与戏剧，同时保留较旧的义项，指任何主题的文献整体。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin stem of letters and writing; the near-meaning group gathers words for stories, poems and written work.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语中「字母、书写」的词干展开；近义组收表示故事、诗歌与文字作品的词。

normalIntro.en: The word grows out of the Latin word for a letter, and its family keeps returning to reading, learning and the works that carry both.

normal.en: Littera is a letter and litteratura is writing made of letters, so literature began as the product of the alphabet.
normal.cn: littera 是字母，litteratura 是由字母写成的文字，所以 literature 最初就是字母的产物。

normal.en: Literature first meant learning gained from books, which is why a literature review still means reading what others have written.
normal.cn: literature 最初指从书本得来的学问，所以文献综述至今仍指阅读别人已经写下的东西。

normal.en: Literary is the adjective and literature the noun: one describes, the other names the whole body of works.
normal.cn: literary 是形容词，literature 是名词：一个作描述，一个指整批作品。

normal.en: A field's literature is the shelf of everything written about it, which is why doctors speak of the literature on a drug.
normal.cn: 一个领域的 literature 就是关于它的全部书面材料，所以医生会说某种药的文献。

normal.en: Promotional literature borrows the prestige of books for leaflets, because print still looks authoritative.
normal.cn: 宣传资料借用了书本的声望来指传单，因为印刷品至今看起来仍然权威。

abstract.en: A library is many voices stored as letters, and literature is the name for that chorus.
abstract.cn: 图书馆是许多声音被存成字母，literature 就是这支合唱的名字。

abstract.en: The same word covers a tragedy and a clinic brochure, because both are printed and meant to be read.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指一部悲剧，也指诊所的小册子，因为两者都是印出来供人阅读的。

abstract.en: Literature is what a culture chooses to keep reading, and that choice changes with each generation.
abstract.cn: 文学是一个文化选择继续阅读的东西，而这个选择会随每一代人改变。

senses.title: A metric unit of volume
senses.definition: a metric unit of volume equal to one cubic decimetre, used for measuring liquids and sometimes grain
senses.definitionCN: 等于一立方分米的公制容量单位，用来计量液体，有时也计量谷物
senses.example: The bottle holds one litre of water.
senses.exampleCN: 这只瓶子能装一升水。
senses.why: The metric system was designed in France, where an older capacity measure called litron supplied the name; the unit was fixed at one cubic decimetre and travelled with the system.
senses.whyCN: 公制在法国设计，当地一种旧的容量单位 litron 提供了名字；这个单位被定为一立方分米，随后随公制传开。

senses.title: The amount contained in one litre
senses.definition: the quantity of liquid or other substance that fills a container of one litre
senses.definitionCN: 装满一升容器所需的液体或其他物质的量
senses.example: She poured a litre of milk into the jug.
senses.exampleCN: 她把一升牛奶倒进壶里。
senses.why: A fixed unit can stand for the quantity it measures: people buy a litre as readily as they buy a metre, so the unit name becomes the name of the amount.
senses.whyCN: 固定的单位可以代替它所量的数量：人们买一升，就像买一米那样自然，于是单位名也成了数量的名字。

intro.en: Litre comes from a French capacity measure, which in turn goes back through Latin to a Greek unit of weight whose earlier origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: litre 来自法国的一种容量单位，再经拉丁语上溯到希腊的一种重量单位，而它更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Greek litra named a Sicilian unit of weight and later a coin; its ultimate origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 希腊语 litra 指西西里的一种重量单位，后来也指钱币；它最终的来源不确定。

items.en: Latin borrowed litra as a name for a small weight or measure, and medieval Latin used it for a measure of capacity.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 litra，指一种小重量或小量具；中世纪拉丁语用它指容量单位。

items.en: Old French litron named a measure of capacity, and French formed litre from it when the metric system was being designed.
items.cn: 古法语 litron 指一种容量单位；法国在设计公制时由它造出了 litre。

items.en: English adopted litre in the nineteenth century together with the metric system and kept the French spelling with -re.
items.cn: 十九世纪英语随公制一起借入 litre，并保留了法语中以 -re 结尾的拼写。

items.en: Modern English uses litre in British spelling and liter in American spelling; both name the same metric unit.
items.cn: 现代英语在英式拼写中用 litre，在美式拼写中用 liter；两者指的是同一个公制单位。

note.cn: 形近组收这个公制单位的拼写变体与倍数单位；近义组收其他用来计量体积的单位。

normal.en: The metric system was built in France, and litre comes from a French measure called litron.
normal.cn: 公制在法国建立，litre 则来自法国一种叫 litron 的量具。

normal.en: Greek litra first named a weight, so the unit began as something weighed rather than something poured.
normal.cn: 希腊语 litra 最初指重量，所以这个单位最早是称出来的，而不是倒出来的。

normal.en: Milli- means a thousandth, so a millilitre is one thousandth of a litre.
normal.cn: milli- 表示千分之一，所以 millilitre 是一升的千分之一。

normal.en: Kilo- means a thousand, so a kilolitre is a thousand litres.
normal.cn: kilo- 表示千，所以 kilolitre 是一千升。

normal.en: The British write litre and Americans write liter, just as theatre and theater differ.
normal.cn: 英国人写 litre，美国人写 liter，就像 theatre 与 theater 的差别一样。

abstract.en: A litre is a cube ten centimetres on each side, a volume you can almost hold in two hands.
abstract.cn: 一升是边长十厘米的立方体，一个几乎能捧在双手里的体积。

abstract.en: The same name can mean the unit and the amount, because measuring and the thing measured are hard to separate.
abstract.cn: 同一个名字既可以指单位，也可以指数量，因为计量行为与被量的东西很难分开。

abstract.en: Every country that sells petrol by the litre is using a measure invented in a French laboratory.

senses.title: Full of energy and enthusiasm
senses.definition: full of energy, movement and enthusiasm, especially in the way a person or animal behaves
senses.definitionCN: 充满精力、动作与热情，尤指人或动物的举止
senses.example: The lively children kept the whole street awake with their shouting.
senses.exampleCN: 这些活泼的孩子用喊声让整条街都醒着。
senses.why: Old English liflic joins lif, life, to -lic, the suffix of likeness; the first sense is a creature visibly full of life, moving and making sound.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 liflic 把 lif（生命）与表示「像……一样」的后缀 -lic 连在一起；最早的义项就是看得见生命在动的活物，会跑会叫。

senses.title: Vivid and full of interest
senses.definition: vivid, interesting and full of imaginative detail, as in a lively description or a lively imagination
senses.definitionCN: 生动有趣、充满想象细节，如生动的描写或丰富的想象力
senses.example: She gave a lively account of the market on a rainy morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她把雨中清晨的集市讲得活灵活现。
senses.why: A description that keeps moving in the mind is felt to have life; the energy of a body is transferred to words, so a vivid account is called lively.
senses.whyCN: 一段在脑海里不断活动的描写会被觉得有生命；身体的能量转移到了文字上，于是生动的叙述就被称作 lively。

senses.title: Busy and full of activity
senses.definition: full of people, movement and excitement, as a place or an event
senses.definitionCN: 充满人群、动静与兴奋感，用来形容地方或活动
senses.example: The square becomes lively after the shops close.
senses.exampleCN: 商店打烊之后，广场就热闹起来。
senses.why: A crowd moves and makes noise like one large body; a place that will not stay quiet borrows the same word.
senses.whyCN: 人群又动又响，像一个巨大的身体；一个安静不下来的地方就借用了同一个词。

senses.title: Bright and strong in colour
senses.definition: of colour, bright and strong enough to catch the eye immediately
senses.definitionCN: 指颜色明亮强烈，一眼就能抓住视线
senses.example: The walls were painted a lively shade of orange.
senses.exampleCN: 墙壁被刷成一种鲜艳的橙色。
senses.why: Strong colour jumps at the eye the way a moving body does; the visual shock is read as a sign of life.
senses.whyCN: 浓烈的颜色像活动的身体一样跳进眼里；这种视觉冲击被读成生命力的标志。

senses.title: Vigorous and full of argument
senses.definition: of a discussion, debate or game, energetic and full of strong, differing views
senses.definitionCN: 指讨论、辩论或比赛充满劲头，带着强烈而不同的意见
senses.example: The proposal led to a lively debate in the council.
senses.exampleCN: 这项提议在议事会里引发了一场激烈的辩论。
senses.why: A debate that keeps returning and refuses to settle behaves like a restless creature; the energy of life is lent to argument.
senses.whyCN: 一场反复回到原点、不肯定论的辩论，举止就像一个停不下来的活物；生命的劲头被借给了争论。

intro.en: Lively began as a Germanic compound meaning life-like, and it gradually shifted from living creatures to vivid speech, bright colour and busy places.
intro.cn: lively 最初是一个意为「像生命一样的」日耳曼语复合词，后来逐渐从活物转到生动的言语、鲜亮的颜色和热闹的地方。

items.en: Old English liflic meant living or having life, built from lif, life, and the suffix -lic.
items.cn: 古英语 liflic 意为有生命的、活着的，由 lif（生命）与后缀 -lic 构成。

items.en: The noun is reconstructed as libam, the ancestor of life; the suffix -lic is related to German -lich and English -ly.
items.cn: 这个词的名词部分一般重构为 libam，是 life 的祖先；后缀 -lic 与德语 -lich、英语 -ly 同源。

items.en: Middle English lively kept the sense living and began to mean active, quick and cheerful.
items.cn: 中古英语的 lively 保留了「活着的」义项，并开始表示活跃、轻快、快活。

items.en: By the sixteenth century lively could describe vivid speech, bright colour and busy places, not only living creatures.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，lively 已能形容生动的言辞、鲜亮的颜色和热闹的地方，不再只用于活物。

items.en: Modern English uses lively mainly for energy and vividness; the older sense of living survives in a few fixed phrases such as a lively hope.
items.cn: 现代英语的 lively 主要用于表示活力与生动；较旧的「活着的」义项只留在少数固定说法里，如 a lively hope。

note.cn: 形近组收建立在日耳曼语「生命」一词上的词；近义组收表示精力、生动与忙碌活动的词。

normalIntro.en: The word joins the Germanic noun for life to a suffix of likeness, and its family keeps returning to living energy and vivid movement.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把日耳曼语中表示「生命」的名词与表示「像……一样」的后缀结合起来，同族词反复回到活着的劲头与生动的动感。

normal.en: Old English liflic is life plus -lic, the suffix that became -ly; lively literally means life-like.
normal.cn: 古英语 liflic 是 life 加 -lic，也就是后来变成 -ly 的那个后缀；lively 字面上就是「像生命一样的」。

normal.en: The same suffix -ly appears in friendly and lovely, turning nouns into adjectives about a quality.
normal.cn: 同一个后缀 -ly 也出现在 friendly 与 lovely 里，把名词变成表示某种性质的形容词。

normal.en: Life, live and alive are close relatives, so a lively room is a room that seems to be alive.
normal.cn: life、live 与 alive 是近亲，所以一间 lively 的屋子就像一间活着的屋子。

normal.en: The word first described a living, moving body, and only later described speech, colour and markets.
normal.cn: 这个词最早描述会动会叫的活物，后来才用来描述言语、颜色和市场。

normal.en: Liveliness adds -ness to lively, naming the quality that a lively person or place shows.
normal.cn: liveliness 在 lively 后加 -ness，用来指活泼的人或地方所表现出的那种性质。

abstract.en: A lively room is one that behaves like a body: it moves, makes sound and will not sit still.
abstract.cn: 一间 lively 的屋子举止像个身体：会动、会响、不肯安静。

abstract.en: We call a description lively when reading it feels like watching something happen.
abstract.cn: 我们把一段描写称作 lively，是因为读它时像在看事情发生。

abstract.en: Bright colour and heated debate share the word because both refuse to stay quiet.
abstract.cn: 鲜艳的颜色与激烈的辩论共用这个词，因为两者都不肯安静。

intro.en: A Germanic noun for life, a suffix of likeness, one Old English adjective and two English suffixes carry lively from a moving body to vivid speech and busy streets.
intro.cn: 一个日耳曼语的生命名词、一个表示「像……一样」的后缀、一个古英语形容词，再加两个英语后缀，把 lively 从活动的身体带到生动的言语与热闹的街道。

senses.title: The organ that cleans the blood
senses.definition: the large reddish-brown organ in the abdomen that removes waste from the blood and stores energy
senses.definitionCN: 腹部内那只红褐色的大器官，负责清除血液中的废物并储存能量
senses.example: The liver processes most of the alcohol taken into the body.
senses.exampleCN: 进入体内的酒精大部分由肝脏处理。
senses.why: Old English lifer named this organ in all three Germanic languages, but why a word for life was used is uncertain; the body part is the fixed centre while the reasons behind the name are disputed.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 lifer 在三种日耳曼语中都用它指这个器官，但为什么用一个与「生命」有关的词来命名则来源不确定；器官本身是固定的核心，命名的原因却存疑。

senses.title: The organ as food
senses.definition: the flesh of an animal's liver eaten as food
senses.definitionCN: 供人食用的动物肝脏
senses.example: She fried the liver with onions and served it hot.
senses.exampleCN: 她把肝和洋葱一起煎好，趁热端上桌。
senses.why: A butcher's counter sells the organ as meat, so the same word quietly moves from anatomy to the plate without needing a second term.
senses.whyCN: 肉摊把这只器官当作肉来卖，于是同一个词从解剖学悄悄移到餐盘上，也不需要另造一个词。

senses.title: A person who lives in a certain way
senses.definition: an old or literary way of naming a person according to the life that person leads
senses.definitionCN: 一种旧式或文学化的说法，按一个人所过的生活来称呼他
senses.example: He was a fast liver, spending his nights in the taverns of the old town.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个放荡的人，夜夜泡在旧城的酒馆里。
senses.why: Once the body word stood for life itself, it could be attached to the adjective for a kind of life; the organ and the person are joined by the idea of living, though the motive of the original name remains uncertain.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个身体词被用来指生活本身，它就能接在表示生活方式的形容词后面；器官与人由「生活」这个概念连在一起，尽管最初命名的动机仍然存疑。

intro.en: Liver is an Old English body word shared by the other Germanic languages, and the reason it carries a sense of life is a matter of debate.
intro.cn: liver 是一个古英语的身体词，其他日耳曼语中也有对应词；它为什么带有「生命」意味，学界仍有争论。

items.en: Lifer appears in Old English medical texts as the name of the organ that breaks down food, and the word is masculine and weak.
items.cn: lifer 见于古英语医学文本，指分解食物的器官，是阳性弱变化名词。

items.en: German Leber and Dutch lever are the same word, and the agreement across the family shows that the body sense is ancient.
items.cn: 德语 Leber 与荷兰语 lever 是同一个词，整个语族的一致表明这个身体义项十分古老。

items.en: The stem looks like the word for life, and OLD ENGLISH LIF is its obvious neighbour, yet scholars have long doubted that the organ was named for life and prefer an earlier unrecorded meaning.
items.cn: 这个词干看起来像「生命」一词，古英语 lif 确实是它显眼的近邻；但学者们早就怀疑这个器官并非由「生命」得名，而更倾向一个更早、未见记载的意思。

items.en: Middle English liber keeps the organ sense and also begins to use the word in the phrase for a person of a certain life.
items.cn: 中古英语的 liber 保留了器官义项，也开始把这个词用在表示某类生活者的说法里。

items.en: Modern English keeps the organ and the meat, drops most of the moralising uses, and lets medicine build terms such as liver disease and liver transplant.
items.cn: 现代英语保留器官与食用肉两个义项，淘汰了多数带道德评判的用法，医学则造出肝病、肝移植等术语。

normalIntro.en: The word is an ancient Germanic name for one organ, and its family keeps returning to the living body and what is taken from it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个古老的日耳曼语器官名称，它的同族词反复回到活着的身体以及从中取出的东西。

normal.en: Old English lifer, German Leber and Dutch lever are the same body word, so the spelling changes little across the family.
normal.cn: 古英语 lifer、德语 Leber 与荷兰语 lever 是同一个身体词，拼写在整个语族里变化很小。

normal.en: Liverwurst comes straight from German Leberwurst, where the first part still means liver.
normal.cn: liverwurst 直接来自德语 Leberwurst，其中第一部分仍然表示肝。

normal.en: The word once worked on its own as a name for a living person, which is why old texts speak of a free liver and a fast liver.
normal.cn: 这个词曾经单独用来称呼活人，所以旧文本里才会出现 free liver、fast liver 之类的说法。

normal.en: Medicine attaches the word to nouns and adjectives, giving liver disease, liver failure and liver transplant.
normal.cn: 医学把这个词接在名词和形容词前，造出 liver disease、liver failure 与 liver transplant。

normal.en: A liver is the only internal organ common enough on a plate to have its own butcher counter and its own recipes.
normal.cn: 肝是唯一常见到能摆上肉摊、还有专属菜谱的内脏器官。

abstract.en: One word covers a hidden organ and a visible slice of meat, a reminder that the body is also something we handle.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指藏起来的器官，又指看得见的一片肉，这提醒人：身体也是我们亲手处理的东西。

abstract.en: The old moral sense links the organ to how a person lives, suggesting that eating and behaviour were once spoken of in one breath.
abstract.cn: 旧的道德义项把器官与人的生活方式连在一起，说明饮食与行为曾经被放在同一口气里谈论。

abstract.en: Every language needs a plain word for the organ that quietly cleans the blood, and English has kept its oldest one.
abstract.cn: 每种语言都需要一个朴素的词来指那个默默清理血液的器官，英语一直留着最古老的那个。

examples.en: The liver processes most of the alcohol taken into the body.
examples.cn: 进入体内的酒精大部分由肝脏处理。

examples.en: She fried the liver with onions and served it hot.
examples.cn: 她把肝和洋葱一起煎好，趁热端上桌。

examples.en: Doctors found that his liver had been damaged by the infection.
examples.cn: 医生发现他的肝已被感染损伤。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「里佛」——肝藏在肚子深处，像个不出声的老佛；记住 liver 是肝脏，也是餐桌上的一片肝。

root: 古英语 lifer（肝）；与德语 Leber、荷兰语 lever 同属一个日耳曼语族。词干貌似与「生命」有关，但更早的命名动机来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The core is one organ inside the body; the senses then divide into the organ itself, the same organ sold as meat, and an old name for a person of a certain life.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是体内的一只器官；义项由此分成器官本身、当作肉出售的同一只器官，以及旧时按生活方式称呼人的说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dark red organ resting on a butcher's block, still wet with a quiet sheen.
core.cn: 核心意象：案板上一块暗红的肝，表面仍带着安静的光泽。

branches.en: a surgeon studying a scan of the abdomen
branches.cn: 外科医生看着腹部影像

branches.en: a butcher weighing a dark red slab on the scale
branches.cn: 屠夫把一块暗红的肝放上秤

branches.en: onions sizzling beside slices of liver
branches.cn: 洋葱在肝片旁滋滋作响

branches.en: a steaming plate set down at a family table
branches.cn: 一盘热气腾腾的菜放上餐桌

branches.en: an old tavern keeper laughing at a regular
branches.cn: 旧酒馆老板冲着熟客笑

intro.en: The word has no Latin ancestry in its body sense; it is a Germanic noun, and English builds only derivatives and compounds on that base.
intro.cn: 这个词的身体义项没有拉丁来源；它是一个日耳曼语名词，英语只在这个词基上造派生词与复合词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; Latin iecur means liver, but the two forms do not share a root.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；拉丁语 iecur 意为「肝」，但两者并不共用一个词根。

definition_zh: 负荷；载荷；载重；负担；装载；加载
definition_en: the weight or force carried by a structure, vehicle or machine, or to put goods, data or a charge into something
core_image: 吊车把一卷钢带挂上吊钩，仪表指针逼近额定值，司机抬手示意停止起升
scene: 吊车把钢卷挂上吊钩，仪表指针逼近额定值，司机抬手示意停止起升。The crane stopped because the load exceeded its rated limit.
sceneCN: 这里指吊具承受的重量（第 1 个义项：结构或吊具承受的载荷）；句意为吊车停了下来，因为载荷超过了额定限度。图中可辨识物件：吊钩、钢卷、载荷仪表、司机、警戒线；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 负荷；载荷；载重；负担
装载；装填；加载

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「装料机；装载者」
由该动词加已然词尾构成，义为「载重的；有负载的」
由该动词加表示进行的名词尾构成，义为「装载；加载」
由表示「超过」的前缀加该词构成，义为「超载」
由表示「取消」的前缀加该动词构成，义为「卸载」

senses.title: The weight a structure carries
senses.definition: the force or weight that a structure, lifting device or machine has to bear
senses.definitionCN: 结构、吊具或机器必须承受的力或重量
senses.example: The beam is designed for a load of ten tonnes.
senses.exampleCN: 这根梁按十吨载荷设计。
senses.why: The word began as a way or a carrying, and engineering fixed it to the weight being carried.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指「路途、承载」，工程语境把它固定到被承载的重量上。

senses.title: The capacity of a vehicle
senses.definition: the amount of goods or weight that a vehicle or vessel is able to carry
senses.definitionCN: 车辆或船舶能够装载的货物量或重量
senses.example: The truck took a full load of gravel.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车装了一整载碎石。
senses.why: A carrying word naturally measures how much can be carried at once.
senses.whyCN: 表示「承载」的词自然用来度量一次能带多少。

senses.title: The weight of work
senses.definition: the amount of work or responsibility a person or system must deal with
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或系统必须处理的工作量或责任
senses.example: The new clerk cut the load on the front desk.
senses.exampleCN: 新来的职员减轻了前台的负担。
senses.why: Work is imagined as goods to be carried, and an extra person shares the load.
senses.whyCN: 工作被想象成要搬运的货物，多一个人就分担了荷载。

senses.title: The demand on a circuit
senses.definition: the power or current drawn by a device or system from a supply
senses.definitionCN: 设备或系统从电源取用的功率或电流
senses.example: The generator tripped when the load doubled.
senses.exampleCN: 负载翻倍时发电机跳闸了。
senses.why: Electrical demand behaves like a weight on a supply, and the old word fitted without change.
senses.whyCN: 用电需求像压在电源上的重量，老词原样就用上了。

senses.title: To put goods on board
senses.definition: to put goods, fuel or material onto a vehicle or into a container
senses.definitionCN: 把货物、燃料或材料放上车船或容器
senses.example: They load the pallets before sunrise.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在日出前把托盘装好。
senses.why: The noun of a burden turned into the verb of placing it, a common British pairing.
senses.whyCN: 「负担」的名词转成「放置负担」的动词，这是英语里常见的名词动化。

senses.title: To charge a weapon or device
senses.definition: to put a charge, film or medium into a weapon, camera or appliance
senses.definitionCN: 把弹药、胶片或介质装入武器、相机或器具
senses.example: He loaded the camera with a fresh roll.
senses.exampleCN: 他给相机装上一卷新胶卷。
senses.why: A device also carries something and needs to be filled before it works.
senses.whyCN: 装置同样要承载东西，用之前必须先填满。

senses.title: To bring data into memory
senses.definition: to transfer a file or program into a computer's memory so that it can be used
senses.definitionCN: 把文件或程序传入计算机内存以便使用
senses.example: The program will load the map on startup.
senses.exampleCN: 程序启动时会加载这张地图。
senses.why: Computing reused the idea of putting something into a carrier before it can act.
senses.whyCN: 计算机沿用「先装进载体才能运作」这个思路。

senses.title: An emotional burden
senses.definition: a weight of worry or responsibility that a person feels
senses.definitionCN: 一个人感受到的忧虑或责任之重
senses.example: She carried a heavy load after the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 事故之后她背负着沉重的心理负担。
senses.why: The body carries weight and the mind borrows the same measure.
senses.whyCN: 身体承担重量，心智借用了同一套度量。

senses.title: The demand on an engine
senses.definition: the amount of power an engine or motor must produce at a given moment
senses.definitionCN: 发动机或电动机在某一时刻必须输出的功率
senses.example: At full load the engine runs at its hottest.
senses.exampleCN: 满负荷时发动机温度最高。
senses.why: Every machine has a working demand, and engineers call that demand its load.
senses.whyCN: 每台机器都有运转需求，工程师把这个需求称作它的负荷。

intro.en: Load goes back to Old English lad, a way or a course, from the reconstructed Proto-Germanic laidō, to go forth. The sense of something carried appeared in Middle English, and the verb followed.
intro.cn: 这个词可追到古英语 lad「路途、进程」，来自原始日耳曼语的重构形式 laidō「向前走」。表示「被承载之物」的意思在中古英语出现，动词随后产生。

items.en: Lad meant a way, a course or a journey, and the earliest sense was about travelling rather than weight.
items.cn: 这个词意为路途、进程或旅程，最早的意思与行走有关，而非重量。

items.en: The Proto-Germanic noun meant a way or a leading, and related forms in other Germanic languages also mean a road or a track.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语名词意为路途或引导，其他日耳曼语中的相关形式也指道路或轨迹。

items.en: By the thirteenth century the word also named what a person or animal carried, and the meaning moved from route to burden; how that shift came about is source uncertain, and one hypothesis links it to a related verb meaning to lead.
items.cn: 到十三世纪，这个词也指人或牲畜背负的东西，意思从路线转向负担；这一语义转变的来源不确定，另有假说认为它受表示「引导、带领」的同族动词影响。

items.en: The verb to put a load on appeared in the fourteenth century, and to load a gun or camera followed later.
items.cn: 表示「给……装货」的动词在十四世纪出现，给枪炮或相机装填的用法随后产生。

items.en: Structural and mechanical engineering gave the noun its precise force sense, and its first attestation date is uncertain.
items.cn: 结构与机械工程赋予这个名词精确的力学含义，首见年代不确定。

items.en: The nineteenth century applied the word to circuits, and the twentieth to data and programs.
items.cn: 十九世纪把它用于电路，二十世纪又用于数据与程序。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like load; the second group names neighbouring ideas of weight and filling.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「load」相近；第二组是与「重量、装载」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: A machine or person that loads material, or a program that loads files.
entries.definitionCN: 指装料的机器或人，也指加载文件的程序。

entries.definition: Carrying a load, or charged with something.
entries.definitionCN: 指载着负荷的，或装填了东西的。

entries.definition: To put more weight or demand on something than it can bear.
entries.definitionCN: 指给某物加上超过其承受能力的重量或需求。

entries.definition: To take goods off a vehicle or remove a burden.
entries.definitionCN: 指把货物从车上卸下或卸去负担。

entries.definition: A vein of ore; it sounds identical but comes from a word for a way or a lead.
entries.definitionCN: 指矿脉；发音相同，但来自表示「路径、引导」的词。

entries.definition: A heavy load, especially one that is hard to carry or bear.
entries.definitionCN: 指沉重的负荷，尤指难以承担的重负。

entries.definition: The heaviness of an object, or a mass placed on something.
entries.definitionCN: 指物体的重量，或放在某物上的质量。

entries.definition: Goods carried by a ship, aircraft or truck.
entries.definitionCN: 指船、飞机或卡车运载的货物。

entries.definition: The part of a vehicle's load that earns revenue or does the work.
entries.definitionCN: 指载具负荷中产生收益或执行任务的那部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real way-word origin, the real trade family and real engineering phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「路途」来源、真实行业同族词与真实工程搭配。

normal.en: Load first meant a road, then the thing a road carries.
normal.cn: load 最初指一条路，后来指这条路所承载的东西。

normal.en: Load capacity and heavy load are the engineering phrases.
normal.cn: 承载能力与重载是工程里的说法。

normal.en: Load a truck, load a camera and load data are three filling acts.
normal.cn: 装车、装胶卷与加载数据是三个「装填」动作。

normal.en: Overload and unload mark too much and none at all.
normal.cn: 超载与卸载标出「太多」与「一点不剩」。

normal.en: Workload is the same weight carried by a person rather than a beam.
normal.cn: 工作量就是由人而不是梁来承担的同一份重量。

abstract.en: A load is a promise the structure must keep every second.
abstract.cn: 载荷是结构每一秒都必须守住的承诺。

abstract.en: The same word weighs a steel coil and a bad memory.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既称钢卷的重量，也称一段坏记忆的重量。

abstract.en: Loading is putting something in so that the thing can begin.
abstract.cn: 加载就是把东西放进去，好让那件事得以开始。

examples.en: The column carries the load of the roof above it.
examples.cn: 这根柱子承受上方屋顶的载荷。

examples.en: Workers load the truck before the gate opens.
examples.cn: 工人在大门打开前装车。

examples.en: The screen froze while the program was loading the file.
examples.cn: 程序加载文件时屏幕卡住了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「漏德」——压在梁上的重量不能「漏」掉，得全「德」扛住：负荷

root: 古英语 lad「路途、进程」← 原始日耳曼语 laidō「向前走」；同族形式多指道路或轨迹。十三世纪起转指所背负之物，十四世纪产生动词，十五世纪用于枪炮装填，十九世纪用于电路，二十世纪用于数据；力学义的确切年代来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all concern what is carried: force on a structure, goods in a vehicle, work on a person, current in a circuit, cargo placed on board, a charge in a device, data in memory, worry in a mind, and power drawn from an engine.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都与「承载」有关：结构受力、车辆载货、人的工作量、电路电流、装船装车、装置装填、内存数据、心中忧虑与发动机输出功率。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hook lifts a coil until the gauge reaches the rated limit.
core.cn: 核心意象：吊钩吊起钢卷，直到仪表到达额定极限。

branches.en: THE FORCE ON A MACHINE: a beam bearing tonnes, and an engine working at full demand.
branches.cn: 机器所受的力：梁承受数吨重量，发动机满负荷运转。

branches.en: THE CARGO: the amount a vehicle can take, and the act of putting it aboard.
branches.cn: 货物：车辆能装的数量，以及把货装上去的动作。

branches.en: THE HUMAN WEIGHT: too much work at a desk, and too much worry in a mind.
branches.cn: 人的重量：桌上过多的工作，与心中过多的忧虑。

branches.en: THE ELECTRICAL DRAW: current taken from a supply until the breaker trips.
branches.cn: 电的取用：从电源取用电流，直到断路器跳闸。

branches.en: THE THING PUT IN: a charge in a weapon, and a file brought into memory.
branches.cn: 装进去的东西：装进武器的弹药，以及带进内存的文件。

intro.en: Load is a native English word of Germanic origin, so it has no Latin ancestor; its Latin list is left empty.
intro.cn: 这是一个日耳曼来源的英语本族词，没有拉丁语祖先，因此拉丁词条留空。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for load; the relevant origin is Proto-Germanic laidō, a word for a way or a course.
latinIntro.cn: load 没有拉丁语来源；相关来源是原始日耳曼语 laidō，指路途或进程。

items.example: The oldest sense is about moving, not carrying.
items.exampleCN: 最古老的意思关乎行走，而非承载。

items.example: The form is reconstructed from related languages.
items.exampleCN: 该形式由相关语言重构而来。

items.example: The compound moves the load from steel to people.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把负荷从钢梁转到人身上。

items.meaning: the earning part of a load
items.meaningCN: 负荷中产生收益的部分
items.example: The compound separates cargo from the vehicle.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把货物与载具分开。

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「装载机；装载者」
由该动词加表示进行的名词尾构成，义为「装载；加载」
由表示「超过」的前缀加该词构成，义为「超载」
由表示「反向」的前缀加该动词构成，义为「卸载」
由「工作」加该名词构成，义为「工作量」

definition_zh: 一条面包；块状食物；游荡；闲混；（俚）脑袋
definition_en: a whole bread baked in one piece, a food shaped into a solid block, to spend time idly, or in British slang the head
core_image: 刚出炉的长条面包摆在木桌上，表皮金黄，被人用手按出一处浅浅的凹痕
scene: 清晨的面包房里，师傅把刚出炉的长条面包一列排开，热气在玻璃上凝成水雾。She cut a thick slice from the loaf and spread it with butter.
sceneCN: 这里 loaf 是「一条面包」（第 1 个义项：整条烤出的面包）；句意为她从整条面包上切下厚厚一片，抹上黄油。图中可辨识物件：木桌、金黄面包、玻璃上的水雾。

pos.zh: 一条面包；块状食物；（俚）脑袋
游荡；闲混；偷懒

derivatives.zh: 由 loaf 加 -er 构成，义为「游手好闲的人」，后又指一种平底船鞋
由 loaf 加 -ing 构成，义为「闲荡；磨洋工」
由 meat 与 loaf 复合，义为「肉糕」，指烤成块状的碎肉

senses.title: A whole bread baked in one piece
senses.definition: a bread baked as one rounded or oblong piece, before it is cut into slices
senses.definitionCN: 烤成一整块、尚未切片的面包，形状多为圆形或长条形
senses.example: She cut a thick slice from the loaf and spread it with butter.
senses.exampleCN: 她从整条面包上切下厚厚一片，抹上黄油。
senses.why: Old English hlaf named bread as a baked whole, and the unit rather than the substance is what the word has always counted.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 hlaf 把面包指认为一整块烤成的东西，这个词从古至今计量的是「一个整体」，而不是面包这种材料。

senses.title: Food pressed into a solid block
senses.definition: food, especially meat or sugar, shaped and cooked into a solid block
senses.definitionCN: 把食物，尤指肉或糖，压成并煮成坚实的块状
senses.example: The meat loaf came out of the oven with a crust of browned fat.
senses.exampleCN: 肉糕出炉时表面结着一层焦黄的油脂。
senses.why: A baked loaf is a mass held together by heat, and cooks reuse that picture whenever they press minced meat or boiled sugar into one solid shape.
senses.whyCN: 烤好的面包是靠热力聚成的一块，厨子把碎肉或熬好的糖压成整块时，便重复了这幅图景。

senses.title: To spend time doing nothing
senses.definition: to pass time without working or without a clear purpose, often while moving about
senses.definitionCN: 不干活、也没有明确目的地消磨时间，常常是四处走动
senses.example: He loafed about the harbour all afternoon, watching the boats come in.
senses.exampleCN: 他整个下午都在港口闲逛，看船进港。
senses.why: The verb appeared centuries after the bread word and its origin is uncertain; it paints idleness as time left to lie around like dough waiting to be shaped.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词比面包那个词晚了好几百年才出现，来源不确定；它把闲散画成一段像面团一样摊着、等着被塑形的时间。

senses.title: The head, in British slang
senses.definition: the head, used in informal British speech and in the phrase use your loaf
senses.definitionCN: 脑袋，用于英式非正式口语，常见于 use your loaf 这一说法
senses.example: Use your loaf and check the timetable before you leave.
senses.exampleCN: 动动脑子，出门前先看看时刻表。
senses.why: Rhyming slang replaced the word for head with a phrase, loaf of bread, and then shortened the phrase to loaf; the bread word thereby acquired a second bodily sense.
senses.whyCN: 押韵俚语用 loaf of bread 这个短语代替「头」这个词，随后又把它缩成 loaf；面包这个词因此多出一个身体义项。

intro.en: Loaf is an Old English word for a baked bread; the verb meaning to idle is much later and its origin is genuinely uncertain.
intro.cn: loaf 是古英语中表示「烤好的面包」的词；表示闲荡的动词出现得晚得多，来源确实不确定。

items.en: Hlaf meant bread as a baked whole, and it also entered compounds for the giver of bread, the hlaford, later lord.
items.cn: hlaf 指一整块烤好的面包，它还进入复合词，用来指分面包的人 hlaford，也就是后来的 lord。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic form is hlaibaz, and German Laib and Gothic hlaifs are its close relatives.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语形式是 hlaibaz，德语 Laib 与哥特语 hlaifs 都是它的近亲。

items.en: Middle English lof keeps the baked sense, and its plural loaves settles the f that turns into v between vowels.
items.cn: 中古英语的 lof 保留「烤好的面包」义，复数 loaves 固定了 f 在两个元音之间变成 v 的规律。

items.en: The verb loaf, meaning to idle, is first recorded in the nineteenth century; dictionaries call its origin uncertain and only suggest a loose link with loiter.
items.cn: 表示闲荡的动词 loaf 最早见于十九世纪；词典称其来源不确定，只提出与 loiter 有松散的关联。

items.en: Modern English adds meat loaf and sugar loaf, and rhyming slang turns loaf of bread into a slang word for the head.
items.cn: 现代英语加上肉糕与糖锥，押韵俚语又把 loaf of bread 变成指脑袋的俚语词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the plural form, one derivative, a German relative and a word that merely looks similar; the near-meaning group collects other bread shapes.
note.cn: 形近组收复数形式、一个派生词、一个德语同族词，以及一个只是拼写相近的词；近义组收其他面包形态的词。

entries.definition: The plural of loaf, with f changed to v before the ending.
entries.definitionCN: loaf 的复数形式，词尾前 f 变为 v。

entries.definition: An idle person, and also a slip-on shoe.
entries.definitionCN: 游手好闲的人；也指一种平底便鞋；由 loaf 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: The German word for a loaf or a round mass of bread.
entries.definitionCN: 德语中表示一条或一块圆形面包的词，与 loaf 同源。

entries.definition: An upper floor or a raised space under a roof; only the spelling is close, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 阁楼；屋顶下的高起空间；与 loaf 只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The baked food made from flour, usually named as a substance rather than counted.
entries.definitionCN: 面粉烤成的食物，通常作为不可数的材料来指称，而 loaf 计量的是整条。

entries.definition: A small round bread, often sweet.
entries.definitionCN: 小圆面包，常带甜味。

entries.definition: A small loaf or bread shaped by rolling the dough.
entries.definitionCN: 小面包；把面团卷成形的面包。

entries.definition: A long narrow French loaf with a crisp crust.
entries.definitionCN: 法式长棍面包；细长、外壳酥脆。

normalIntro.en: The word starts as bread counted by the piece, and its family keeps returning to baked masses, idle time and one slang head.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词最初是把面包按「个」来数，它的同族词反复回到烤成的块、闲散的时间，以及一个俚语里的脑袋。

normal.en: Old English hlaf meant a baked bread, and the same root gave hlaford, the bread giver who became the lord.
normal.cn: 古英语 hlaf 指烤好的面包，同一个词根还给出 hlaford，即分面包的人，后来成为 lord。

normal.en: German Laib and Gothic hlaifs are close cousins, so the bread sense is shared across the Germanic family.
normal.cn: 德语 Laib 与哥特语 hlaifs 是近亲，面包义项在整个日耳曼语族中相通。

normal.en: The plural loaves shows the old rule that f becomes v between two vowels, as in leaf and leaves.
normal.cn: 复数 loaves 体现了 f 在两个元音之间变 v 的古老规则，就像 leaf 与 leaves 一样。

normal.en: Meat loaf and sugar loaf borrow the shape of a baked block, not the bread itself.
normal.cn: meat loaf 与 sugar loaf 借的是烤成的一块这个形状，而不是面包本身。

normal.en: To use your loaf is rhyming slang: loaf of bread stood for head, and the phrase was cut down to one word.
normal.cn: use your loaf 属于押韵俚语：loaf of bread 代替 head，后来整个短语被缩成一个词。

abstract.en: A loaf is bread treated as a single object, which is why the word counts pieces while bread names a material.
abstract.cn: loaf 是把面包当成一个整体物件，所以它数「条」，而 bread 指的是材料。

abstract.en: The same word for a solid baked block later describes a person standing about doing nothing, as if time itself were dough.
abstract.cn: 同一个表示烤成实心块的词，后来用来形容人站着什么都不做，仿佛时间本身也是面团。

abstract.en: English took the sound of a bread phrase and made it a word for the mind, showing how slang can carry a body part on a bakery image.
abstract.cn: 英语借一个面包短语的声音造出指头脑的词，说明俚语能让身体部位搭在烘焙的意象上。

examples.en: She cut a thick slice from the loaf and spread it with butter.
examples.cn: 她从整条面包上切下厚厚一片，抹上黄油。

examples.en: He loafed about the harbour all afternoon, watching the boats come in.
examples.cn: 他整个下午都在港口闲逛，看船进港。

examples.en: Use your loaf and check the timetable before you leave.
examples.cn: 动动脑子，出门前先看看时刻表。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「老富」——老富有钱却不肯干活，整天在街上晃；loaf 是游荡，也是一条面包。

root: 古英语 hlaf（烤好的面包），与德语 Laib、哥特语 hlaifs 同源；表示「闲荡」的动词晚出，来源不确定，一般认为可能与 loiter 有松散关联。

sensesIntro.en: The core is one baked bread; the senses then divide into food pressed into a block, the later verb for idling, and a rhyming-slang head.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一整条烤好的面包；义项由此分成压成块的食物、晚出的闲荡动词，以及押韵俚语里的脑袋。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a golden loaf on a wooden board, one thumb print pressed into its warm crust.
core.cn: 核心意象：木板上一条金黄的面包，温热的外皮上按着一个拇指印。

branches.en: a baker sliding fresh loaves onto a cooling rack
branches.cn: 面包师把新出炉的面包放上晾架

branches.en: a meat loaf steaming beside a knife
branches.cn: 肉糕冒着热气，旁边放着刀

branches.en: a cone of hard sugar standing on a counter
branches.cn: 柜台上立着一个硬糖锥

branches.en: a man drifting past closed shop fronts
branches.cn: 一个人晃过一间间关门的店铺

branches.en: a friend tapping his temple in a joke
branches.cn: 朋友开玩笑地敲了敲太阳穴

intro.en: The word is a Germanic noun for baked bread, and English stacks a plural, an agent suffix and compounds on that base.
intro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语中表示烤面包的名词，英语在这个词基上加上复数、施事后缀与复合词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; Latin panis means bread, but it is a different root with no shared ancestry.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；拉丁语 panis 意为「面包」，但那是另一个词根，并无共同来源。
